prompt: If $\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{x}{20}$, what is the value of $x$?
hint: The two fractions are equal, so the top and bottom of the first were scaled by the same number. Compare the two denominators.

hints.text: The two fractions are equal, so the top and bottom of the first were scaled by the same number. Compare the two denominators.
The denominator $4$ became $20$, which is $5$ times as large. Multiply the numerator $3$ by the same factor.

explanation: Cross-multiply the proportion to get $3 \times 20 = 4x$, which simplifies to $60 = 4x$.
Divide both sides by $4$ to isolate the variable, giving $x = 15$.
Scaling confirms it: the denominator was multiplied by $5$, and $3 \times 5 = 15$. The value of $x$ is $15$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Scaling beats cross-multiplying when it is clean
steps: Whenever one denominator divides evenly into the other, scaling is faster and involves no division.
Here $20 \div 4 = 5$, so multiply the top by $5$.
Save cross-multiplication for the cases where the numbers do not cooperate.
